title: Factoring Trigonometric Equations
subject: mathematics

theory.introduction: Some trigonometric equations can be factored using familiar algebraic techniques before solving each factor.

content.text: If a product equals zero, at least one factor must equal zero. This allows a complicated trigonometric equation to be separated into simpler equations.
Move all terms to one side, factor the expression, solve each factor, and combine all valid solutions.

examples.question: Solve 2sin²(x) − sin(x) = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
examples.solution: Factor: sin(x)(2sin(x) − 1) = 0. Thus sin(x) = 0 or sin(x) = 1/2. The solutions are 0, π, π/6, and 5π/6.

key_ideas: Treat trigonometric expressions algebraically when possible.
Factor before applying more complicated identities.
misconceptions: Dividing by sin(x) and accidentally removing sin(x) = 0 solutions.
